rules.rule_name: Card File Open for Sequential Reading
rules.rule_description: Before any card records can be read and displayed, the Card File (CARDFILE-FILE) must be successfully opened for sequential input reading.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
2:Card File Open
Open CARDFILE-FILE for sequential reading

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program has announced its start and is ready to process card records
acceptance_criteria.When: The program attempts to open the Card File (CARDFILE-FILE) for sequential reading
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Card File is opened for input access, making all card records available for sequential retrieval

rules.rule_name: Card File Open Success Validation
rules.rule_description: The program must verify that the Card File was successfully opened before proceeding to read any card records. If the file cannot be opened, processing cannot continue.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
File Open
Successful?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program has attempted to open the Card File (CARDFILE-FILE) for sequential reading
acceptance_criteria.When: The file open operation completes and the file status is evaluated
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the file status is successful (status code '00'), the program proceeds to the card file processing loop; if the file status indicates any failure (any status other than '00'), the program triggers an error reporting and abnormal termination sequence

rules.rule_name: Card File Open Error Reporting
rules.rule_description: When the Card File cannot be opened, the program must report the failure with a descriptive error message and the specific file status details to support problem diagnosis.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
9:Error Reporting
Display 'ERROR OPENING CARDFILE'
Display IO Status Message

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program attempted to open the Card File (CARDFILE-FILE) and the open operation failed
acceptance_criteria.When: The file open failure is detected
acceptance_criteria.Then: The program displays the message 'ERROR OPENING CARDFILE', followed by the file status indicator message in the format 'FILE STATUS IS: NNNN' with the specific status value appended, before proceeding to abnormal termination

rules.rule_name: Abnormal Program Termination on Card File Open Failure
rules.rule_description: When the Card File cannot be opened, the program must terminate abnormally with a specific abend code to signal a critical failure to the operations team.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
10:Abnormal Program Termination
Abend Program with Code 999

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Card File open operation has failed and the error message has been displayed
acceptance_criteria.When: The program invokes the abnormal termination routine
acceptance_criteria.Then: The program calls the system abend routine 'CEE3ABD' with abend code 999 and timing value 0, causing an immediate abnormal program termination

rules.rule_name: Card File Processing Loop - End of File Check
rules.rule_description: The program must continuously read and display card records in a loop, checking after each read cycle whether the end of the Card File has been reached to determine if processing should continue or stop.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
6:Card File Processing Loop
End of File Reached?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Card File has been successfully opened and the program is in the card record processing loop
acceptance_criteria.When: The end-of-file flag is evaluated at the start of each loop iteration
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the end-of-file flag is 'N' (not reached), the program proceeds to read the next card record; if the end-of-file flag is 'Y' (end reached), the program exits the loop and proceeds to close the Card File

rules.rule_name: Sequential Card Record Read
rules.rule_description: Within the processing loop, the program reads the next available card record sequentially from the Card File into the card record data area.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
3:Sequential Card Record Read
Read next card record from CARDFILE-FILE

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Card File is open, the end-of-file flag is 'N', and the program is inside the card file processing loop
acceptance_criteria.When: The program reads the next record from the Card File (CARDFILE-FILE) into the CARD-RECORD data area
acceptance_criteria.Then: The card record data is loaded into CARD-RECORD and the file status is set to reflect the outcome of the read operation (successful read, end of file, or read error)

rules.rule_name: End-of-File Detection After Card Record Read
rules.rule_description: After each card record read attempt, the program must determine whether the end of the Card File was reached or a valid record was retrieved, to decide whether to display the record or exit the loop.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
4:End-of-File Detection
Is EOF flag set?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program has attempted to read the next card record from the Card File
acceptance_criteria.When: The file status returned from the read operation is evaluated
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the file status is successful (status code '00'), the end-of-file flag remains 'N' and the program proceeds to display the card record; if the file status indicates end of file (status code '10'), the end-of-file flag is set to 'Y' and the program returns to the loop condition check without displaying a record; if the file status indicates any other error condition, the program triggers read error reporting and abnormal termination

rules.rule_name: Card Record Display
rules.rule_description: Each successfully retrieved card record must be displayed in full, presenting all card data contained within the record.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
5:Card Record Display
Display Card Number and Card Data

acceptance_criteria.Given: A card record has been successfully read from the Card File and the end-of-file flag is still 'N'
acceptance_criteria.When: The program processes the successfully retrieved card record
acceptance_criteria.Then: The complete contents of the CARD-RECORD (including card number and all card data fields) are displayed to the output

rules.rule_name: Card File Read Error Reporting
rules.rule_description: When an unexpected error occurs while reading a card record (not an end-of-file condition), the program must report the failure with a descriptive error message and the specific file status details.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program attempted to read the next card record from the Card File and the read operation returned a status other than successful (status '00') or end-of-file (status '10')
acceptance_criteria.When: The read error condition is detected
acceptance_criteria.Then: The program displays the message 'ERROR READING CARDFILE', followed by the file status indicator message in the format 'FILE STATUS IS: NNNN' with the specific status value appended, before proceeding to abnormal termination

rules.rule_name: Abnormal Program Termination on Card File Read Error
rules.rule_description: When an unexpected error occurs while reading a card record, the program must terminate abnormally with a specific abend code to signal a critical failure.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:

acceptance_criteria.Given: A card file read error has occurred and the error message has been displayed
acceptance_criteria.When: The program invokes the abnormal termination routine
acceptance_criteria.Then: The program calls the system abend routine 'CEE3ABD' with abend code 999 and timing value 0, causing an immediate abnormal program termination

rules.rule_name: Card File Close After Processing Completion
rules.rule_description: After all card records have been read and displayed (end of file reached), the Card File must be properly closed to complete the processing cycle.

rules.rule_name: Open Card Data File for Sequential Reading
rules.rule_description: The Card Data File must be opened for sequential reading before any card records can be accessed or processed. This is the mandatory first step in the card file processing workflow.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Attempt to Open Card Data File for Sequential Reading

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Card Data File (CARDFILE-FILE) is available and the program is starting its card record processing workflow
acceptance_criteria.When: The program initiates the Card Data File open operation for sequential reading (INPUT mode)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Card Data File is prepared and made available for sequential record-by-record reading, allowing the program to proceed with processing all card records

rules.rule_name: Card File Open Success Validation
rules.rule_description: After attempting to open the Card Data File, the program must verify whether the open operation completed successfully. A successful open means the file is ready for processing; any other outcome is treated as a failure.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Was File Opened Successfully?

acceptance_criteria.Given: An attempt has been made to open the Card Data File for sequential reading
acceptance_criteria.When: The file system returns a response to the open request — either a successful open confirmation (file status '00') or any other status indicating a failure
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the file status is '00' (successful), the Card Data File is marked as ready for processing and the program continues normally; if the file status is anything other than '00', the open is treated as a failure and error handling is triggered

rules.rule_name: Card File Ready for Processing
rules.rule_description: When the Card Data File has been successfully opened, it is confirmed as ready and the program proceeds to the card record reading and display workflow without any interruption.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Card File Ready for Processing

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Card Data File open operation has been attempted
acceptance_criteria.When: The file open response confirms success (file status equals '00'), meaning the file is accessible and positioned at the first record
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Card Data File is confirmed as ready for sequential record processing, and the program proceeds to the main card record reading loop without displaying any messages or errors

rules.rule_name: Display Error Notification on Card File Open Failure
rules.rule_description: When the Card Data File cannot be opened successfully, the program must immediately notify the user or operator with a clear error message identifying that the Card File open operation has failed.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Display Error Message: 'ERROR OPENING CARDFILE'

acceptance_criteria.Given: An attempt has been made to open the Card Data File for sequential reading
acceptance_criteria.When: The file open operation fails — the file status returned is anything other than '00' (successful)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The program displays the error message 'ERROR OPENING CARDFILE' to alert the operator that the Card Data File could not be opened and processing cannot continue

rules.rule_name: Display Detailed File Status Information on Open Failure
rules.rule_description: Following the error notification for a Card File open failure, the program must display detailed file status information to assist in diagnosing the root cause of the failure. This provides additional context beyond the simple error message.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Display Detailed File Status Information

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Card Data File open operation has failed and the error message 'ERROR OPENING CARDFILE' has been displayed
acceptance_criteria.When: The program proceeds to report the detailed status of the failed file operation by invoking the file status display routine (9910-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS), which formats and displays the file status code — handling both numeric status codes (displayed as a 4-character formatted status in the pattern 'FILE STATUS IS: NNNN' followed by the status value) and non-numeric or system-specific status codes (where the first status character and a binary-converted second status character are combined and displayed in the same 'FILE STATUS IS: NNNN' pattern)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The detailed file status information is displayed to the operator, providing the specific status code that caused the open failure to support problem diagnosis and resolution

rules.rule_name: Abnormal Program Termination on Card File Open Failure
rules.rule_description: When the Card Data File cannot be opened, the program cannot perform its core function of reading and displaying card records. Therefore, after reporting the error and file status details, the program must terminate abnormally to signal that processing did not complete successfully.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Terminate Program Abnormally

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Card Data File open operation has failed, the error message has been displayed, and the detailed file status information has been shown
acceptance_criteria.When: The program invokes the abnormal termination routine (9999-ABEND-PROGRAM), which calls the system abnormal termination service 'CEE3ABD' with an abort code of 999
acceptance_criteria.Then: The program terminates abnormally with abort code 999, displaying 'ABENDING PROGRAM' before termination, signaling to the operator and any calling processes that the Card File processing job has failed and did not complete successfully — no card records are read or displayed

acceptance_criteria.Then: The operation result is marked as an error, the message 'ERROR READING CARDFILE' is displayed, and the file status details are captured and displayed to identify the nature of the read failure

acceptance_criteria.Then: The program terminates abnormally immediately, halting all further card record processing to prevent any incomplete or erroneous data from being processed or displayed

rules.sub_graph_node_text: Was Read Successful? Status = 00

acceptance_criteria.Given: A read operation has been attempted on the Card File to retrieve the next card record
acceptance_criteria.When: The Card File returns a successful read status indicating the record was retrieved without any issues
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system marks the operation result as successful (result code = 0), confirming the card record is available and valid for display and processing

acceptance_criteria.Then: The system marks the operation result as an end-of-file condition (result code = 16), signaling that all card records have been processed and no further reads should be attempted

rules.rule_name: Signal End of Card Processing Loop
rules.rule_description: When the end of the Card File is detected, the system sets the End-of-File flag to YES to formally signal that all card records have been read and the processing loop should be terminated.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Signal End of Processing - Set End-of-File Flag to YES

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has determined that the Card File has reached its end-of-file condition (result code = 16)
acceptance_criteria.When: The end-of-file result is confirmed after the read attempt
acceptance_criteria.Then: The End-of-File flag is set to YES, formally signaling that all card records have been exhausted and no further card records are available for processing

rules.rule_name: Unexpected Card File Read Error Reporting and Termination

rules.sub_graph_node_text: Report Read Error - Display Error Message

acceptance_criteria.Given: A read operation on the Card File has failed and the failure is not due to reaching the end of the file
acceptance_criteria.When: An unexpected error condition is detected during the card record read attempt
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system displays the message 'ERROR READING CARDFILE', displays the detailed file status information to assist in diagnosing the issue, and immediately triggers an abnormal program termination (abend) to halt all further processing

rules.rule_name: Exit Card Processing Loop When All Records Are Read
rules.rule_description: The card record processing loop continuously checks the End-of-File flag before each iteration. Once the flag is set to YES, the loop exits immediately, ensuring no further read attempts are made after all card records have been processed.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Exit Processing Loop - No More Cards to Read

acceptance_criteria.Given: The card record processing loop is actively running and evaluating whether more records need to be processed
acceptance_criteria.When: The End-of-File flag has been set to YES, indicating that all card records in the Card File have been read and displayed
acceptance_criteria.Then: The processing loop exits immediately without attempting any further card record reads, and control passes to the Card File closure step

rules.rule_name: Continue Processing Next Card Record When File Not Exhausted

acceptance_criteria.Then: The successfully retrieved card record is displayed, and the processing loop continues to attempt reading the next card record from the Card File

acceptance_criteria.Then: The card record display step is skipped entirely, no card data is output, and control returns to the processing loop to allow it to terminate

acceptance_criteria.When: The program attempts to retrieve the next card record from the Card File
acceptance_criteria.Then: The next card record is read from the Card File and stored in the Card Record data area, and the read result status is evaluated to determine the next action

rules.rule_name: Display Card Record Upon Successful Read
rules.rule_description: When a card record is successfully retrieved from the Card File, the complete card record — including card number and all card data — is displayed. The loop then continues to check for the next record.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Display Card Record Card Number and Card Data

acceptance_criteria.Given: A read operation has been performed on the Card File and the End-of-File flag remains 'N' after the read
acceptance_criteria.When: The card record is confirmed as successfully retrieved (read status is successful and end-of-file flag is not set)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The complete Card Record is displayed, and the loop iterates back to check the End-of-File flag for the next read cycle

rules.rule_name: Detect End-of-File Condition and Stop Card Record Processing
rules.rule_description: When a read attempt returns an end-of-file indicator (no more card records exist in the file), the End-of-File flag is set to signal that all card records have been processed. The loop then re-evaluates the flag and exits cleanly.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is End of File Detected?

acceptance_criteria.Given: A read operation has been performed on the Card File and the read did not return a successful record
acceptance_criteria.When: The read result indicates that the end of the Card File has been reached (file status is end-of-file)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The End-of-File flag is set to 'Y', the loop re-evaluates the flag, determines EOF is reached, and exits the loop to proceed with Card File closure — no card record is displayed

rules.rule_name: Handle Card File Read Failure with Error Display and Program Termination
rules.rule_description: When a card record read operation fails for any reason other than a normal end-of-file condition, an error message is displayed along with the file status details, and the program is immediately terminated abnormally to prevent further incorrect processing.

acceptance_criteria.Given: A read operation has been performed on the Card File and the read did not return a successful record
acceptance_criteria.When: The read result indicates an unexpected failure — neither a successful read nor a normal end-of-file condition
acceptance_criteria.Then: The message 'ERROR READING CARDFILE' is displayed, the Card File status details are displayed, and the program is immediately terminated abnormally — no further card records are read or displayed

acceptance_criteria.Then: The Card File is closed to finalize the processing session

rules.rule_name: Card File Close Operation Must Complete Successfully
rules.rule_description: The Card File close operation must be verified for success. A successful close confirms the Card File processing session has ended cleanly with no data integrity issues.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Close Operation Successful?

acceptance_criteria.Given: A close operation has been attempted on the Card File

acceptance_criteria.Then: The Card File close process ends normally and program execution continues to completion

rules.rule_name: Card File Close Failure Must Be Reported as an Error

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program has successfully completed reading all card records from the Card File and has closed the Card File without errors

rules.rule_name: Display Operation-Specific Error Message on File Operation Failure
rules.rule_description: When a Card File operation (open, read, or close) fails, the system must immediately display a descriptive error message that identifies which specific operation encountered the failure, so that the nature of the problem is clearly communicated.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Display Operation-Specific Error Message e.g. ERROR OPENING/READING/CLOSING CARDFILE

acceptance_criteria.Given: A Card File operation (open, read, or close) has been attempted and has resulted in a failure condition
acceptance_criteria.When: The error reporting process is triggered by the failed file operation
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must display a specific error message corresponding to the failed operation: 'ERROR OPENING CARDFILE' if the failure occurred during file open, 'ERROR READING CARDFILE' if the failure occurred during file read, or 'ERROR CLOSING CARDFILE' if the failure occurred during file close

rules.rule_name: Capture Current File Status Code at Point of Failure
rules.rule_description: At the moment a Card File operation fails, the current file status code must be captured and preserved so it can be formatted and displayed as part of the error report.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Capture Current File Status Code

acceptance_criteria.Given: A Card File operation has failed and the operation-specific error message has been displayed
acceptance_criteria.When: The error reporting process proceeds to capture the failure details
acceptance_criteria.Then: The current Card File status code must be captured from the Card File status indicator and stored in the IO Status field for subsequent formatting and display

rules.rule_name: Classify File Status as Vendor-Specific or Standard for Error Formatting
rules.rule_description: Before formatting the file status for display, the system must determine whether the captured status code represents a vendor-specific or non-standard error condition versus a standard numeric file status, as each type requires a different formatting approach.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is File Status Non-Numeric OR Status starts with '9'?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Card File status code has been captured into the IO Status field following a file operation failure
acceptance_criteria.When: The error reporting process evaluates the nature of the status code
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the IO Status value is non-numeric OR the first character of the IO Status (IO-STAT1) is '9', the status is classified as a vendor-specific or special status and must be formatted using the vendor-specific method; otherwise, if the IO Status is fully numeric and does not start with '9', it is classified as a standard status and must be formatted using the standard numeric method

rules.rule_name: Format Vendor-Specific or Non-Numeric File Status for Error Display
rules.rule_description: When the file status is identified as vendor-specific or non-numeric, it must be formatted using a binary conversion method to accurately represent the status code in a displayable 4-character format, preserving the full meaning of the vendor-specific status.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Format Status as Vendor-Specific Code Using Binary Conversion

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Card File status code has been classified as vendor-specific or non-numeric (IO Status is non-numeric OR IO-STAT1 equals '9')
acceptance_criteria.When: The vendor-specific status formatting process is applied
acceptance_criteria.Then: The first character of the IO Status (IO-STAT1) must be placed in the first position of the 4-character display status field (IO-STATUS-04); the second character of the IO Status (IO-STAT2) must be converted through a binary representation (setting a two-byte binary field to zero, moving IO-STAT2 into the right byte, then moving the binary value to the status display sub-field IO-STATUS-0403) to produce the final 4-character formatted status code ready for display

rules.rule_name: Format Standard Numeric File Status for Error Display
rules.rule_description: When the file status is identified as a standard numeric code, it must be formatted into a 4-character display field by padding with leading zeros and placing the 2-character status in the last two positions, producing a consistent 4-digit display format.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Format Status as Standard 4-Digit Numeric Code

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Card File status code has been classified as a standard numeric status (IO Status is fully numeric AND IO-STAT1 does not equal '9')
acceptance_criteria.When: The standard numeric status formatting process is applied
acceptance_criteria.Then: The 4-character display status field (IO-STATUS-04) must first be initialized to '0000', and then the 2-character IO Status value must be placed into positions 3 and 4 of the display field, resulting in a zero-padded 4-digit representation of the standard file status code

rules.rule_name: Display Formatted File Status Error Message
rules.rule_description: After the file status code has been formatted (either as vendor-specific or standard numeric), the system must display the formatted status code with a standard label so that the exact failure status is visible and meaningful to the user or operator.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Display Formatted File Status Message 'FILE STATUS IS: NNNN' + Status Code

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Card File status code has been formatted into the 4-character display field (IO-STATUS-04) using either the vendor-specific or standard numeric formatting method
acceptance_criteria.When: The final step of the error reporting process executes
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must display the message 'FILE STATUS IS: NNNN' immediately followed by the 4-character formatted status code (IO-STATUS-04), providing the complete error status information before returning control to the calling file operation handler

rules.rule_name: Abnormal Program Termination on Critical Card File Error
rules.rule_description: When a critical and unrecoverable error occurs during card file processing (any file operation failure that is neither a successful operation nor a normal end-of-file condition), the program must notify operators of the abnormal termination and immediately abort execution with a designated termination code.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Critical File Error Detected

acceptance_criteria.Given: The card file processing is in progress (either during open, read, or close operations) AND a critical file error has been detected that is not a normal end-of-file condition
acceptance_criteria.When: The file operation status is neither successful (status 00) nor end-of-file (status 10), indicating an unrecoverable file error has occurred
acceptance_criteria.Then: The program must: (1) Display the message 'ABENDING PROGRAM' to notify operators that the program is terminating abnormally, (2) Set the abnormal termination code to 999 to mark the program for abnormal end, and (3) Terminate the program immediately and abnormally — no further card file records are read or displayed, and normal end-of-program processing is bypassed

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Card File Reader program CBACT02C is invoked

all_rules.Rule_Name: Program Initialization Announcement
all_rules.Rule_Description: The program must announce its start before any card file processing begins, providing a clear audit trail marker for the beginning of execution.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program has announced its start and is ready to process card records
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program attempts to open the Card File (CARDFILE-FILE) for sequential reading
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Card File is opened for input access, making all card records available for sequential retrieval

all_rules.Rule_Name: Card File Open for Sequential Reading
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before any card records can be read and displayed, the Card File (CARDFILE-FILE) must be successfully opened for sequential input reading.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program has attempted to open the Card File (CARDFILE-FILE) for sequential reading
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The file open operation completes and the file status is evaluated
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the file status is successful (status code '00'), the program proceeds to the card file processing loop; if the file status indicates any failure (any status other than '00'), the program triggers an error reporting and abnormal termination sequence

all_rules.Rule_Name: Card File Open Success Validation
all_rules.Rule_Description: The program must verify that the Card File was successfully opened before proceeding to read any card records. If the file cannot be opened, processing cannot continue.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program attempted to open the Card File (CARDFILE-FILE) and the open operation failed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The file open failure is detected
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program displays the message 'ERROR OPENING CARDFILE', followed by the file status indicator message in the format 'FILE STATUS IS: NNNN' with the specific status value appended, before proceeding to abnormal termination

all_rules.Rule_Name: Card File Open Error Reporting
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Card File cannot be opened, the program must report the failure with a descriptive error message and the specific file status details to support problem diagnosis.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Card File open operation has failed and the error message has been displayed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program invokes the abnormal termination routine
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program calls the system abend routine 'CEE3ABD' with abend code 999 and timing value 0, causing an immediate abnormal program termination

all_rules.Rule_Name: Abnormal Program Termination on Card File Open Failure
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Card File cannot be opened, the program must terminate abnormally with a specific abend code to signal a critical failure to the operations team.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Card File has been successfully opened and the program is in the card record processing loop
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The end-of-file flag is evaluated at the start of each loop iteration
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the end-of-file flag is 'N' (not reached), the program proceeds to read the next card record; if the end-of-file flag is 'Y' (end reached), the program exits the loop and proceeds to close the Card File

all_rules.Rule_Name: Card File Processing Loop - End of File Check
all_rules.Rule_Description: The program must continuously read and display card records in a loop, checking after each read cycle whether the end of the Card File has been reached to determine if processing should continue or stop.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Card File is open, the end-of-file flag is 'N', and the program is inside the card file processing loop
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program reads the next record from the Card File (CARDFILE-FILE) into the CARD-RECORD data area
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The card record data is loaded into CARD-RECORD and the file status is set to reflect the outcome of the read operation (successful read, end of file, or read error)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Sequential Card Record Read
all_rules.Rule_Description: Within the processing loop, the program reads the next available card record sequentially from the Card File into the card record data area.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program has attempted to read the next card record from the Card File
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The file status returned from the read operation is evaluated
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the file status is successful (status code '00'), the end-of-file flag remains 'N' and the program proceeds to display the card record; if the file status indicates end of file (status code '10'), the end-of-file flag is set to 'Y' and the program returns to the loop condition check without displaying a record; if the file status indicates any other error condition, the program triggers read error reporting and abnormal termination

all_rules.Rule_Name: End-of-File Detection After Card Record Read
all_rules.Rule_Description: After each card record read attempt, the program must determine whether the end of the Card File was reached or a valid record was retrieved, to decide whether to display the record or exit the loop.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A card record has been successfully read from the Card File and the end-of-file flag is still 'N'
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program processes the successfully retrieved card record
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The complete contents of the CARD-RECORD (including card number and all card data fields) are displayed to the output

all_rules.Rule_Name: Card Record Display
all_rules.Rule_Description: Each successfully retrieved card record must be displayed in full, presenting all card data contained within the record.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program attempted to read the next card record from the Card File and the read operation returned a status other than successful (status '00') or end-of-file (status '10')
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The read error condition is detected
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program displays the message 'ERROR READING CARDFILE', followed by the file status indicator message in the format 'FILE STATUS IS: NNNN' with the specific status value appended, before proceeding to abnormal termination

all_rules.Rule_Name: Card File Read Error Reporting
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an unexpected error occurs while reading a card record (not an end-of-file condition), the program must report the failure with a descriptive error message and the specific file status details.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A card file read error has occurred and the error message has been displayed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program invokes the abnormal termination routine
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program calls the system abend routine 'CEE3ABD' with abend code 999 and timing value 0, causing an immediate abnormal program termination

all_rules.Rule_Name: Abnormal Program Termination on Card File Read Error
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an unexpected error occurs while reading a card record, the program must terminate abnormally with a specific abend code to signal a critical failure.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The end-of-file flag has been set to 'Y', indicating all card records have been processed, and the program has exited the processing loop
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program executes the Card File close operation
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Card File (CARDFILE-FILE) is closed and the file status is set to reflect the outcome of the close operation

all_rules.Rule_Name: Card File Close After Processing Completion
all_rules.Rule_Description: After all card records have been read and displayed (end of file reached), the Card File must be properly closed to complete the processing cycle.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program has attempted to close the Card File (CARDFILE-FILE) after completing all record processing
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The file close operation completes and the file status is evaluated
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the file status is successful (status code '00'), the program proceeds to display the program completion message; if the file status indicates any failure (any status other than '00'), the program triggers an error reporting and abnormal termination sequence

all_rules.Rule_Name: Card File Close Success Validation
all_rules.Rule_Description: The program must verify that the Card File was successfully closed after all records have been processed. A failure to close the file is treated as a critical error.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program attempted to close the Card File (CARDFILE-FILE) and the close operation failed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The file close failure is detected
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program displays the message 'ERROR CLOSING CARDFILE', followed by the file status indicator message in the format 'FILE STATUS IS: NNNN' with the specific status value appended, before proceeding to abnormal termination

all_rules.Rule_Name: Card File Close Error Reporting
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Card File cannot be properly closed after processing, the program must report the failure with a descriptive error message and the specific file status details.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Card File close operation has failed and the error message has been displayed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program invokes the abnormal termination routine
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program calls the system abend routine 'CEE3ABD' with abend code 999 and timing value 0, causing an immediate abnormal program termination

all_rules.Rule_Name: Abnormal Program Termination on Card File Close Failure
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Card File cannot be properly closed, the program must terminate abnormally with a specific abend code to signal a critical failure.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: All card records have been successfully read and displayed, and the Card File has been successfully closed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program reaches its normal completion point
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program displays the message 'END OF EXECUTION OF PROGRAM CBACT02C' and terminates normally

all_rules.Rule_Name: Program Completion Announcement
all_rules.Rule_Description: Upon successful completion of all card file processing and file closure, the program must announce its normal end to provide a clear audit trail marker for the completion of execution.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Card Data File Reading program CBACT02C has been invoked and is ready to begin execution
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program starts its execution before performing any file operations or data processing
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program must display the message 'START OF EXECUTION OF PROGRAM CBACT02C' to confirm that execution has commenced, after which the program proceeds to open the Card File

all_rules.Rule_Name: Program Execution Start Announcement
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before any card data file processing begins, the program must announce its start of execution by displaying a start message. This ensures traceability and confirms the program has been initiated successfully.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Card Data File (CARDFILE-FILE) is available and the program is starting its card record processing workflow
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program initiates the Card Data File open operation for sequential reading (INPUT mode)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Card Data File is prepared and made available for sequential record-by-record reading, allowing the program to proceed with processing all card records

all_rules.Rule_Name: Open Card Data File for Sequential Reading
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Card Data File must be opened for sequential reading before any card records can be accessed or processed. This is the mandatory first step in the card file processing workflow.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An attempt has been made to open the Card Data File for sequential reading
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The file system returns a response to the open request — either a successful open confirmation (file status '00') or any other status indicating a failure
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the file status is '00' (successful), the Card Data File is marked as ready for processing and the program continues normally; if the file status is anything other than '00', the open is treated as a failure and error handling is triggered

all_rules.Rule_Name: Card File Open Success Validation
all_rules.Rule_Description: After attempting to open the Card Data File, the program must verify whether the open operation completed successfully. A successful open means the file is ready for processing; any other outcome is treated as a failure.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Card Data File open operation has been attempted
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The file open response confirms success (file status equals '00'), meaning the file is accessible and positioned at the first record
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Card Data File is confirmed as ready for sequential record processing, and the program proceeds to the main card record reading loop without displaying any messages or errors

all_rules.Rule_Name: Card File Ready for Processing
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Card Data File has been successfully opened, it is confirmed as ready and the program proceeds to the card record reading and display workflow without any interruption.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An attempt has been made to open the Card Data File for sequential reading
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The file open operation fails — the file status returned is anything other than '00' (successful)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program displays the error message 'ERROR OPENING CARDFILE' to alert the operator that the Card Data File could not be opened and processing cannot continue

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Error Notification on Card File Open Failure
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Card Data File cannot be opened successfully, the program must immediately notify the user or operator with a clear error message identifying that the Card File open operation has failed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Card Data File open operation has failed and the error message 'ERROR OPENING CARDFILE' has been displayed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program proceeds to report the detailed status of the failed file operation by invoking the file status display routine (9910-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS), which formats and displays the file status code — handling both numeric status codes (displayed as a 4-character formatted status in the pattern 'FILE STATUS IS: NNNN' followed by the status value) and non-numeric or system-specific status codes (where the first status character and a binary-converted second status character are combined and displayed in the same 'FILE STATUS IS: NNNN' pattern)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The detailed file status information is displayed to the operator, providing the specific status code that caused the open failure to support problem diagnosis and resolution

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Detailed File Status Information on Open Failure
all_rules.Rule_Description: Following the error notification for a Card File open failure, the program must display detailed file status information to assist in diagnosing the root cause of the failure. This provides additional context beyond the simple error message.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Card Data File open operation has failed, the error message has been displayed, and the detailed file status information has been shown
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program invokes the abnormal termination routine (9999-ABEND-PROGRAM), which calls the system abnormal termination service 'CEE3ABD' with an abort code of 999
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program terminates abnormally with abort code 999, displaying 'ABENDING PROGRAM' before termination, signaling to the operator and any calling processes that the Card File processing job has failed and did not complete successfully — no card records are read or displayed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Abnormal Program Termination on Card File Open Failure
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Card Data File cannot be opened, the program cannot perform its core function of reading and displaying card records. Therefore, after reporting the error and file status details, the program must terminate abnormally to signal that processing did not complete successfully.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Card File has been successfully opened and is ready for sequential reading, and the End-of-File flag is set to 'N' indicating records may still be available
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program requests the next card record sequentially from the Card File
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The next card record is retrieved from the Card File and loaded into the card record memory area, making it available for display and processing

all_rules.Rule_Name: Sequential Read of Next Card Record from Card File
all_rules.Rule_Description: The program reads the next available card record sequentially from the Card File, one record at a time, loading it into memory for further processing.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A sequential read operation has been performed on the Card File
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Card File returns a successful read status indicating the record was retrieved without any issues
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The card record is confirmed as successfully loaded into memory, the operation result is marked as successful (AOK), and the record is ready to be displayed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Successful Card Record Retrieval Confirmation
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a card record is read without any errors, the record is confirmed as successfully loaded into memory and is marked as ready for display.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A sequential read operation has been performed on the Card File and the read was not successful
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Card File returns an end-of-file status indicating there are no more records to be read
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The operation result is marked as End-of-File (EOF), signaling that all card records have been processed and no more records are available

all_rules.Rule_Name: End-of-File Detection During Card Record Read
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a read attempt on the Card File does not return a record successfully, the program determines whether the condition is a normal end-of-file or an unexpected error.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A sequential read operation has been performed on the Card File and the end-of-file condition has been detected
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program confirms that the end-of-file status has been reached with no more card records available
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The End-of-File flag is set to 'Y', which will cause the card record processing loop to exit on its next iteration check, stopping all further card record reads

all_rules.Rule_Name: End-of-File Flag Set to Stop Card Record Processing
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the end of the Card File is reached, the End-of-File flag is set to 'Y' to signal the processing loop to stop reading and exit gracefully.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A sequential read operation has been performed on the Card File, the read was not successful, and the condition is not a normal end-of-file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Card File returns an unexpected error status that is neither a successful read nor an end-of-file condition
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The operation result is marked as an error, the message 'ERROR READING CARDFILE' is displayed, and the file status details are captured and displayed to identify the nature of the read failure

all_rules.Rule_Name: Unexpected Card File Read Error Detection
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a card record read fails for any reason other than a normal end-of-file, the program identifies it as an unexpected read error and displays a descriptive error message along with the file status details.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An unexpected error has occurred during a card record read operation, the error message 'ERROR READING CARDFILE' and file status details have been displayed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program determines the card file read error is unrecoverable and cannot continue processing
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program terminates abnormally immediately, halting all further card record processing to prevent any incomplete or erroneous data from being processed or displayed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Program Termination on Unrecoverable Card File Read Error
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an unexpected and unrecoverable error occurs while reading a card record, the program terminates abnormally to prevent processing of incomplete or corrupt data.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A read operation has been attempted on the Card File to retrieve the next card record
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Card File returns a successful read status indicating the record was retrieved without any issues
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system marks the operation result as successful (result code = 0), confirming the card record is available and valid for display and processing

all_rules.Rule_Name: Successful Card Record Read Confirmation
all_rules.Rule_Description: After attempting to read a card record, the system confirms whether the read operation completed successfully, marking the record as available for display and further processing.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A read operation on the Card File did not return a successful status, meaning no new card record was retrieved
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Card File signals that there are no more records to read, indicating the end of the file has been reached
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system marks the operation result as an end-of-file condition (result code = 16), signaling that all card records have been processed and no further reads should be attempted

all_rules.Rule_Name: End of Card File Detection
all_rules.Rule_Description: After an unsuccessful card record read, the system determines whether the failure was due to reaching the natural end of the Card File, distinguishing a normal completion condition from an unexpected error.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has determined that the Card File has reached its end-of-file condition (result code = 16)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The end-of-file result is confirmed after the read attempt
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The End-of-File flag is set to YES, formally signaling that all card records have been exhausted and no further card records are available for processing

all_rules.Rule_Name: Signal End of Card Processing Loop
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the end of the Card File is detected, the system sets the End-of-File flag to YES to formally signal that all card records have been read and the processing loop should be terminated.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A read operation on the Card File has failed and the failure is not due to reaching the end of the file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: An unexpected error condition is detected during the card record read attempt
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system displays the message 'ERROR READING CARDFILE', displays the detailed file status information to assist in diagnosing the issue, and immediately triggers an abnormal program termination (abend) to halt all further processing

all_rules.Rule_Name: Unexpected Card File Read Error Reporting and Termination
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a card record read fails for any reason other than a normal end-of-file, the system reports the error with a descriptive message and the file status details, then immediately terminates the program abnormally to prevent further incorrect processing.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The card record processing loop is actively running and evaluating whether more records need to be processed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The End-of-File flag has been set to YES, indicating that all card records in the Card File have been read and displayed
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The processing loop exits immediately without attempting any further card record reads, and control passes to the Card File closure step

all_rules.Rule_Name: Exit Card Processing Loop When All Records Are Read
all_rules.Rule_Description: The card record processing loop continuously checks the End-of-File flag before each iteration. Once the flag is set to YES, the loop exits immediately, ensuring no further read attempts are made after all card records have been processed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A card record read attempt has been completed and the End-of-File flag status is being evaluated
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The End-of-File flag remains set to NO after the read, confirming a valid card record was successfully retrieved
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The successfully retrieved card record is displayed, and the processing loop continues to attempt reading the next card record from the Card File

all_rules.Rule_Name: Continue Processing Next Card Record When File Not Exhausted
all_rules.Rule_Description: After a successful card record read, the system verifies the End-of-File flag is still set to NO before displaying the record, ensuring only valid, fully retrieved records are displayed and the loop continues to the next card.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A read operation has been performed on the Card File and a result has been returned
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates whether the End-of-File flag is set to 'No', indicating a real card record was successfully retrieved
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the End-of-File flag is 'No', the card record is considered valid and eligible for display; if the End-of-File flag is 'Yes', the record is not valid and display is skipped

all_rules.Rule_Name: Validate Card Record Availability Before Display
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before displaying a card record, the system must verify that the record retrieved is a valid, non-end-of-file record. Only records confirmed as available (End-of-File flag is 'No') are eligible for display. This rule prevents display of a non-existent record when the end of the Card File has been reached.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A card record has been successfully retrieved from the Card File and the End-of-File flag is confirmed as 'No'
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system processes the valid card record for output
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The complete card record details, including the card number and all associated card data contained within the record, are displayed to the output

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Valid Card Record Details
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a valid card record has been confirmed as available (End-of-File is 'No'), the complete card record — including the card number and all associated card data — must be displayed to the output. This is the core business output action of the program.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A read operation has been performed on the Card File and the End-of-File flag has been set to 'Yes', indicating no further card records are available
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates the End-of-File flag and finds it is not 'No'
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The card record display step is skipped entirely, no card data is output, and control returns to the processing loop to allow it to terminate

all_rules.Rule_Name: Skip Card Record Display When End of File Is Reached
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Card File signals that there are no more records to process (End-of-File condition is detected), the display step must be bypassed entirely. No output is produced for the end-of-file condition itself, and control returns to the processing loop which will then terminate.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A successful read operation has populated the card record storage area with data from the Card File
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The End-of-File flag is confirmed as 'No', indicating the card record storage area contains valid card data
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The card record storage area, containing the card number and all associated card data as read directly from the Card File, is used as the source for display output

all_rules.Rule_Name: Extract Card Details from Retrieved Card Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a valid card record is confirmed as available, the card details — comprising the card number and all associated card data — are sourced directly from the card record that was read from the Card File into the card record storage area during the retrieval step.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Card File processing loop is active and the End-of-File flag is being evaluated
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The End-of-File flag is checked at the start of each loop iteration
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the End-of-File flag is set to 'Y', the loop terminates and processing proceeds to close the Card File; if the End-of-File flag is 'N', the program proceeds to read the next card record

all_rules.Rule_Name: Evaluate End-of-File Status Before Reading Next Card Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before attempting to read the next card record, the program checks whether the end of the Card File has already been reached. If the end-of-file flag is set, no further reading is attempted and the loop exits to proceed with file closure.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Card File is open for reading and the End-of-File flag is 'N'
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program attempts to retrieve the next card record from the Card File
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The next card record is read from the Card File and stored in the Card Record data area, and the read result status is evaluated to determine the next action

all_rules.Rule_Name: Read Next Card Record from Card File
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the end of file has not been reached, the program reads the next sequential card record from the Card File into the Card Record data area for further processing.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A read operation has been performed on the Card File and the End-of-File flag remains 'N' after the read
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The card record is confirmed as successfully retrieved (read status is successful and end-of-file flag is not set)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The complete Card Record is displayed, and the loop iterates back to check the End-of-File flag for the next read cycle

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Card Record Upon Successful Read
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a card record is successfully retrieved from the Card File, the complete card record — including card number and all card data — is displayed. The loop then continues to check for the next record.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A read operation has been performed on the Card File and the read did not return a successful record
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The read result indicates that the end of the Card File has been reached (file status is end-of-file)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The End-of-File flag is set to 'Y', the loop re-evaluates the flag, determines EOF is reached, and exits the loop to proceed with Card File closure — no card record is displayed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Detect End-of-File Condition and Stop Card Record Processing
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a read attempt returns an end-of-file indicator (no more card records exist in the file), the End-of-File flag is set to signal that all card records have been processed. The loop then re-evaluates the flag and exits cleanly.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A read operation has been performed on the Card File and the read did not return a successful record
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The read result indicates an unexpected failure — neither a successful read nor a normal end-of-file condition
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The message 'ERROR READING CARDFILE' is displayed, the Card File status details are displayed, and the program is immediately terminated abnormally — no further card records are read or displayed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Handle Card File Read Failure with Error Display and Program Termination
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a card record read operation fails for any reason other than a normal end-of-file condition, an error message is displayed along with the file status details, and the program is immediately terminated abnormally to prevent further incorrect processing.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: All card records have been read and displayed from the Card File
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The end of the Card File has been reached and the read loop has completed
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Card File is closed to finalize the processing session

all_rules.Rule_Name: Card File Must Be Closed After All Records Are Processed
all_rules.Rule_Description: After all card records have been read and displayed, the Card File must be formally closed to complete the processing cycle.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A close operation has been attempted on the Card File
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Card File close operation returns a successful completion status
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Card File close process ends normally and program execution continues to completion

all_rules.Rule_Name: Card File Close Operation Must Complete Successfully
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Card File close operation must be verified for success. A successful close confirms the Card File processing session has ended cleanly with no data integrity issues.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A close operation has been attempted on the Card File
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Card File close operation does not return a successful completion status
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The error message 'ERROR CLOSING CARDFILE' is displayed, followed by a detailed file status message showing the specific status code in the format 'FILE STATUS IS: NNNN' with the actual status value appended

all_rules.Rule_Name: Card File Close Failure Must Be Reported as an Error
all_rules.Rule_Description: If the Card File cannot be closed successfully, a descriptive error message must be displayed along with the detailed file status information to identify the nature of the failure.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Card File close operation has failed and the error details have been displayed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The close failure error reporting is complete
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program is immediately terminated abnormally by invoking the abnormal termination routine with termination code 999

all_rules.Rule_Name: Program Must Terminate Abnormally When Card File Cannot Be Closed
all_rules.Rule_Description: A failure to close the Card File is a critical error condition that requires immediate abnormal termination of the program to prevent data loss or corruption.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program has successfully completed reading all card records from the Card File and has closed the Card File without errors
Acceptance_Criteria.When: All card records have been processed and displayed, and the Card File has been closed successfully
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program displays the message 'END OF EXECUTION OF PROGRAM CBACT02C' to confirm successful completion of the card data file reading and printing process, and then returns control to the calling system

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Program Completion Message
all_rules.Rule_Description: Upon successful completion of reading and displaying all card records from the Card File, the program must display a message confirming the end of execution before returning control to the calling system.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A Card File operation (open, read, or close) has been attempted and has resulted in a failure condition
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The error reporting process is triggered by the failed file operation
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must display a specific error message corresponding to the failed operation: 'ERROR OPENING CARDFILE' if the failure occurred during file open, 'ERROR READING CARDFILE' if the failure occurred during file read, or 'ERROR CLOSING CARDFILE' if the failure occurred during file close

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Operation-Specific Error Message on File Operation Failure
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a Card File operation (open, read, or close) fails, the system must immediately display a descriptive error message that identifies which specific operation encountered the failure, so that the nature of the problem is clearly communicated.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A Card File operation has failed and the operation-specific error message has been displayed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The error reporting process proceeds to capture the failure details
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The current Card File status code must be captured from the Card File status indicator and stored in the IO Status field for subsequent formatting and display

all_rules.Rule_Name: Capture Current File Status Code at Point of Failure
all_rules.Rule_Description: At the moment a Card File operation fails, the current file status code must be captured and preserved so it can be formatted and displayed as part of the error report.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Card File status code has been captured into the IO Status field following a file operation failure
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The error reporting process evaluates the nature of the status code
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the IO Status value is non-numeric OR the first character of the IO Status (IO-STAT1) is '9', the status is classified as a vendor-specific or special status and must be formatted using the vendor-specific method; otherwise, if the IO Status is fully numeric and does not start with '9', it is classified as a standard status and must be formatted using the standard numeric method

all_rules.Rule_Name: Classify File Status as Vendor-Specific or Standard for Error Formatting
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before formatting the file status for display, the system must determine whether the captured status code represents a vendor-specific or non-standard error condition versus a standard numeric file status, as each type requires a different formatting approach.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Card File status code has been classified as vendor-specific or non-numeric (IO Status is non-numeric OR IO-STAT1 equals '9')
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The vendor-specific status formatting process is applied
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The first character of the IO Status (IO-STAT1) must be placed in the first position of the 4-character display status field (IO-STATUS-04); the second character of the IO Status (IO-STAT2) must be converted through a binary representation (setting a two-byte binary field to zero, moving IO-STAT2 into the right byte, then moving the binary value to the status display sub-field IO-STATUS-0403) to produce the final 4-character formatted status code ready for display

all_rules.Rule_Name: Format Vendor-Specific or Non-Numeric File Status for Error Display
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the file status is identified as vendor-specific or non-numeric, it must be formatted using a binary conversion method to accurately represent the status code in a displayable 4-character format, preserving the full meaning of the vendor-specific status.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Card File status code has been classified as a standard numeric status (IO Status is fully numeric AND IO-STAT1 does not equal '9')
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The standard numeric status formatting process is applied
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The 4-character display status field (IO-STATUS-04) must first be initialized to '0000', and then the 2-character IO Status value must be placed into positions 3 and 4 of the display field, resulting in a zero-padded 4-digit representation of the standard file status code

all_rules.Rule_Name: Format Standard Numeric File Status for Error Display
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the file status is identified as a standard numeric code, it must be formatted into a 4-character display field by padding with leading zeros and placing the 2-character status in the last two positions, producing a consistent 4-digit display format.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Card File status code has been formatted into the 4-character display field (IO-STATUS-04) using either the vendor-specific or standard numeric formatting method
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The final step of the error reporting process executes
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must display the message 'FILE STATUS IS: NNNN' immediately followed by the 4-character formatted status code (IO-STATUS-04), providing the complete error status information before returning control to the calling file operation handler

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Formatted File Status Error Message
all_rules.Rule_Description: After the file status code has been formatted (either as vendor-specific or standard numeric), the system must display the formatted status code with a standard label so that the exact failure status is visible and meaningful to the user or operator.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The card file processing is in progress (either during open, read, or close operations) AND a critical file error has been detected that is not a normal end-of-file condition
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The file operation status is neither successful (status 00) nor end-of-file (status 10), indicating an unrecoverable file error has occurred
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program must: (1) Display the message 'ABENDING PROGRAM' to notify operators that the program is terminating abnormally, (2) Set the abnormal termination code to 999 to mark the program for abnormal end, and (3) Terminate the program immediately and abnormally — no further card file records are read or displayed, and normal end-of-program processing is bypassed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Abnormal Program Termination on Critical Card File Error
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a critical and unrecoverable error occurs during card file processing (any file operation failure that is neither a successful operation nor a normal end-of-file condition), the program must notify operators of the abnormal termination and immediately abort execution with a designated termination code.

description:
CBACT02C is a batch COBOL program within the CardDemo application that sequentially reads all records from an indexed card data file and displays each card record to the output. The program opens the card file, iterates through every record printing its contents, and closes the file upon completion. It is a standalone main/driver program with no external program calls other than an abend utility.
- **Execution Environment**: Batch - **Database Access**: VSAM (Indexed) - **MQ Calls**: No - **Module Type**: Main/Driver module
### Key Functionalities: 1: Program Initialization - Display a message indicating the start of the card data file reading process 2: Card File Open - Open the card data file for sequential reading to prepare for processing all card records 3: Sequential Card Record Read - Read the next card record sequentially from the card data file one record at a time 4: End-of-File Detection - Detect when all card records have been read and signal the end of processing loop 5: Card Record Display - Display each card record's details (card number and associated card data) to the output 6: Card File Processing Loop - Continuously read and display all card records from the file until the end of file is reached 7: Card File Close - Close the card data file after all records have been read and displayed 8: Program Completion - Display a message indicating the successful end of the card data file reading and printing process 9: Error Reporting - Display a meaningful error status message when a failure occurs during file open, read, or close operations 10: Abnormal Program Termination - Terminate the program abnormally when a critical file error is encountered during card file processing
